messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: High tail latency detected on /v1/generate (hosted). 95th pct latency spiked to 920ms over the last 5m, queue depth rising on batchers.
Alex K: oncall here, investigating. link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency
Alex K: paging @Maya P (primary oncall next) and @Lee S for SRE triage
Maya P: on it. can you paste the top node error logs? any model changes?
Alex K: no deploys in last 30m, suspect traffic shape. snippets from batcher logs:

```
[batcher-3] queued=120 inflight=48 max_batch_wait_ms=20 avg_batch_size=2.1
[batcher-3] dispatch_delay_ms=85 token_throughput_drop=0.34
```

Lee S: looks like small batches => high per-token overhead. throughput down, latency up. Are we seeing a surge of low-latency single-turn requests? support, any customer complaints?
Rachel S: support reports 3 enterprise customers noticing timeouts on long prompts (>=1024 tokens). A couple of freemium customers showing 429 spikes.
Juan R: runtime note: continuous batching default max_wait_ms = 20. If we increase to 80-120ms we can combine more requests and recover throughput but will add p50/p95 latency. Suggest temporary increase to 100ms.
Alex K: propose mitigations in order:
1) increase continuous batching max_wait_ms to 100ms (runtime config)
2) temporarily tighten per-user rate limit for free tier (reduce from 60 qpm to 20 qpm)
3) route non-enterprise traffic to model-micro-1 (lower-cost, compatible) for 10m burn-in
4) monitor errors and revert when queue depth normalizes

Maya P: +1. I'll make the runtime change and apply traffic shaping. Alex, can you handle the rate-limit patch and notify support to message impacted customers?
Alex K: applying rate-limit change now:

```
# deploy rate limit patch
curl -XPOST https://control.redwood/api/quotas
 -d '{"tier":"free","qpm":20}' 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```

deploy-bot: rate-limit update accepted (change_id: rl-202911-7b)
Alex K: runtime change command:

```
rwctl runtime update --component=batcher --set continuous_batching.max_wait_ms=100
```

deploy-bot: rolling update started for batcher (28 nodes)
deploy-bot: 12/28 nodes updated

Lee S: started routing rule to divert non-enterprise traffic to model-micro-1 using policy 'soft-shape-2029'
Juan R: also lowered default max_tokens to 1024 for free tier until stable to limit long prompts
Rachel S: I've posted an advisory to support channel and flagged 4 enterprise accounts for proactive outreach.
Maya P: monitoring dashboards: queue depth dropping, avg_batch_size up from 2.1 -> 6.5, token throughput recovering

```
metric: avg_batch_size
before: 2.1
after: 6.5
p95_latency_before: 920ms
p95_latency_after: 1180ms
```

Maya P: note p95 increased to ~1.18s (expected), but p50 improved slightly. Tradeoff accepted to stop timeouts.
Alex K: support: send friendly note to freemium customers about temporary rate limits and to enterprise accounts that we're mitigating and will follow up.
Rachel S: sending notices now. templates used: /templates/mitigation-rate-limit.md

Lee S: keeping emergency runbook open. If error rate rises or CPU on batchers >85%, we'll rollback to 20ms and open an incident bridge.
Maya P: handing off to @Maya P for the 30m watch. Summary for next oncall:
- Why: small-batch surge causing throughput collapse
- Actions: increased max_wait_ms to 100, tightened free-tier qpm to 20, routed non-enterprise to model-micro-1, lowered free max_tokens
- Impact: p95 latency up ~260ms, fewer timeouts, reduced 429s for enterprise
- Next steps: monitor dashboards, prepare rollback if CPU high or errors spike

Alex K: thanks all. I'll annotate the incident in pagerduty and add details to the postmortem bucket.
Maya P: taking over watch. ping me if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
